content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper discusses a somewhat novel task setting, online few-shot segmentation, where a stream of images is supplied to a model, with masks of previously seen images presented to the model one step after the corresponding images are segmented. The paper proposes the use of prototype memory, test-time adaptation with variational inference method, and memory-augmented segmentation to address the gap between conventional Few-Shot Segmentation (FSS) and this novel task setting. Combined, the method shows some level of improvement from baseline methods in the proposed task setting.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
- The paper introduces a novel task setting, online few-shot segmentation, which is a more realistic task setting than conventional FSS. The motivation of the proposed task setting is well-articulated.

- The proposed method demonstrates better performance than baselines on two well-established FSS datasets and a medical segmentation dataset.

Weaknesses

- Though storing prototypes is more efficient than storing raw examples, the proposed prototype memory grows unbounded in an $O(N)$ rate w.r.t. the number of seen samples, which causes memory usage to grow $O(N)$ and transformer computation time to grow $O(N^2)$. This contradicts the online setting where the segmentation model can observe thousands of examples. In contrast, many methods that investigate online learning settings (e.g., continual learning methods such as [1, 2]) have a way of selecting a subset of representative samples (Algorithm 1 in both papers).

- The ablation studies in Tables 1, 2, 3, and 4 seem to be either unfair (i.e., use bad baselines) or unclear.

    - In table 1, the baseline setting w/o Prototype memory is implemented by using only the prototype estimated from the last sample, which effectively reduces the model to be always performing 1-shot learning from the last sample (this is also evident from the similar performance regardless of the number of shots). Why not use a moving average of prototypes? In addition, why would the two methods differ in the 1-shot case where the prototype memory is exactly the prototype from the last sample?

    - Table 2 does not seem to be ablating the variational inference module. Instead, the ‘deterministic’ classifier seems to only set L=1 in Monte Carlo sampling. It is not clear how the posterior supervision (i.e., red arrows in Figure 2) affects the training dynamics. Additionally, why do bolded numbers reported in the row ‘variational classifier’ differ from bolded numbers reported in Tables 1 and 3?

    - In table 3, the paper claims that the baseline is achieved by realizing Eq. (2). But it is unclear how this is implemented.

    - In table 4, why replace Eq. 5 with the prototype from the last sample? Why not set $m_i = 1$ in Eq. 5?

- The use of variational inference, which is claimed to be one of the major contributions, is not well justified both theoretically and empirically.

    - Theoretically, the paper proposes to use variational inference for test-time adaptation and formulate classifier weights as latent variables in variational inference, which is not very well motivated. Why is variational inference preferable to other test-time adaptation techniques such as self-supervised learning or test-time augmentation?

    - Empirically, as discussed in the previous point, table 2 fails to ablate the effect of variational inference. The effect of variational inference is unclear from provided experiments.

[1] Cha, Sungmin, et al. "SSUL: Semantic Segmentation with Unknown Label for Exemplar-based Class-Incremental Learning." NeurIPS. 2021.

[2] Bang, Jihwan, et al. "Rainbow memory: Continual learning with a memory of diverse samples." CVPR. 2021.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The proposed task setting is well-motivated and well-articulated, but the presentation of the method can be improved for better clarity.

- Based on the implementation details in the supplementary materials, it seems that the authors use a meta-learning-like training paradigm like conventional FSS by sampling episodes of sequences from the training classes. The clarity of the work could be improved if the authors could point out this formulation prior to discussing technical details.

- Some important details are missing, which create ambiguity for reproduction. For instance, in sec 2.2 it was mentioned that the prior distribution $p$ and the posterior distribution $q$ are modeled generated by transformers. Are these two distributions modeled by two different models? Or are they modeled by the same transformer that shares weight, by with different number of query tokens?
content.summary_of_the_review: In summary, I am leaning towards the negative side due to the lack of comprehensive experiments and insufficient justification of the use of variational inference, which is claimed to be one of the main technical contributions of this work. I am rating empirical novelty as 2 due to my doubts about the fairness of ablations, but I am open to discussion if the authors can kindly provide more details.

content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, the authors propose a memory-augmented variational adaptation method for online few-shot segmentation (i.e., every new sample arrives sequentially). They formulate the adaption process as a variational Bayesian inference problem. Specifically, the sample and prototype memory are regarded as conditions, and the proposed method aims to obtain sample-specific parameters. Meanwhile, a memory-augmented segmentation scheme is applied to learn sample-specific representations. Finally, the proposed method is test on two natural image datasets and one medical image dataset.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

Overall, the proposed method is reasonable and is devised for online few-shot segmentation tasks. Experiments show that all three innovation components, i.e. prototype memory, variational test-time adaptation and memory-augmented segmentation, have achieved promising performance compared to the baseline model. 

Weaknesses:

- The writing of this manuscript can be further improved. The novelty of the proposed three components may not be well explained. Meanwhile, it is also hard to understand the technical details of the proposed method. 

- The experimental results may not be solid enough. Although I understand that online few-shot learning (especially samples come in sequentially) is different from conventional few-shot learning tasks, the authors may still need to compare the proposed method with conventional few-shot methods to demonstrate the advantages of the proposed methods (and task).  As a few-shot learning method, the experimental results reported in the paper should be further improved.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This manuscript clearly explained the authors' motivation and solutions. However, the clarity of the proposed methods may be further improved.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, this work made a reasonable attempt to solve online few-shot segmentation tasks. My main concern is the paper's quality can be further improved. Detailed comments pls refer strength and weaknesses.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a novel few-shot segmentation scenario , i.e., online few-shot segmentation, and a corresponding method named memory-augmented variational adaptation. The online few-shot segmentation emphasizes that the support samples for novel classes do not appear at once, but arrive in sequence. The memory-augmented variational adaptation consists of online class prototype generation for training, variational test-time adaptation and probabilistic classifier. The authors claim that these components jointly help the model to better cope with the sample diversity, therefore improving the adaptation to the online-arriving samples.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
**Strength**
The paper is generally clear. 

**Weakness**
- The motivation for investigating online FSS  is not convincing. The major characteristic of FSS (and other few-shot learning tasks) is that there are very limited support samples. The cost for collecting these few-shot support samples is very low. What reasons make you think it is necessary to  receive the support samples sequentially instead of batching them together? 
- There is another problem with the proposed online FSS setting. In the second paragraph in INTRODUCTION, the authors state that "the model evaluation and updating proceed alternatively". This setting is unnecessary either, since you do not use the evaluation on the preorder evaluation result to adjust the following annotation (e.g., in the active learning manner). In other words, since the annotations for different samples are independent from each other, alternative evaluation and model updating is not necessary for this task, buy may only serve as an efficient implementation for evaluation. So why do you emphasize this setting?
-  In the *t*-th time step, can the deep model revisit all the samples that previously arrived (i.e., $x_1$ to $x_{t-1}$, and their corresponding labels )？

      -- If the answer is negative, what the reason to prohibit such revisiting? The online setting only assumes that samples arrive sequentially, but should not prohibit revisiting the samples that already arrived. 
      
      -- If the answer is positive, then why not using all the samples (i.e., $x_1$ to $x_t$) that already arrived for updating the model?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper is generally clear and easy to understand. 
Although the proposed scenario and the corresponding solution seem novel, the newly-proposed scenario is ill-posed.
content.summary_of_the_review: The authors should provide reasons for the necessity for the online setting of FSS.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper investigates online few-shot segmentation making dense predictions for novel classes with sequential samples. Compared with traditional few-shot segmentation (FSS) tasks revealing all images and annotations simultaneously, online FSS obtains samples along the time series. To address the above problem, The authors propose a novel model consisting of prototype memory, variational test-time adaption, and memory-augmented segmentation in this paper.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. Brief and concise paper writing. 

2. Propose new points of view and perspectives to solve few-shot segmentation in the actual application scenario.

3. Sufficient experiments prove the effectiveness of different proposed components.



Drawbacks and questions:

1. The first line of ABSTRACT: "We investigate online few-show segmentation..." ->It should be "few-shot" instead of "few-show".

2. This paper investigates the online few-shot segmentation, which proposes a new setting that deals with sequential samples. So why online-learning is essential for few-shot learning? Few-shot segmentation predicts the query masks with only a handful of support annotations. So even when new samples are supplemented, we can directly extend the support set instead of retraining the model.

3. At each time point, a pair of the new image and the last annotated mask is provided to the model for online learning. Does it mean we have to annotate the previous image every time? If the time is too long, the annotation workload will become very large and against the original intention of few-shot learning. Conventional few-shot segmentation only needs one or at most five images with annotations.

4. If the time series is too long, many images and annotations exist. The problem becomes the standard semantic segmentation instead of few-shot learning.

5. The experiments prove the effectiveness of the test-time adaptation. The time complexity and time consumption still need to provide. Online learning may cause time consumption and cannot be applied to practical problems.

6. The proposed model's performance is dissatisfied under the standard few-shot segmentation setting compared with recent work in this area.

7. What are the advantages compared with the conventional few-shot segmentation model? For each time point, we can add the new annotation with the previous image into the support set, forming one-shot, two-shot, and three-shot... to segment the new query image.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The clarity is satisfying, but the quality and novelty are with concerns as discussed in the weakness section.
content.summary_of_the_review:
My major concerns are related to the necessity of the newly proposed setting. Also, the experimental section should also be supplemented with more information to make the paper more solid. The authors please give responses to my questions mentioned in the previous section. 

Given the current quality that does not meet the demanding standard of ICLR, my rating is REJECT.

content.title: Memory-Augmented Variational Adaptation for Online Few-Shot Segmentation
content.abstract: We investigate online few-show segmentation, which learns to make dense predictions for novel classes while observing samples sequentially. The main challenge in such an online scenario is the sample diversity in the sequence, resulting in models that do not generalize well to future samples. To this end, we propose a memory-augmented variational adaptation mechanism, which learns to adapt the model to every new sample that arrives sequentially. Specifically, we first introduce a prototype memory, which retains category knowledge from previous samples to facilitate the model adaptation to future samples.  The adaptation to each new sample is then formulated as a variational Bayesian inference problem, which strives to generate sample-specific model parameters by conditioning the sample and the prototype memory. Furthermore, we propose memory-augmented  segmentation to learn sample-specific feature representation for better adaptation to the segmentation of each sample. With extensive experiments, we show that a simple extension of existing few-shot segmentation methods tends to converge to over-smoothed, averaged masks of lesser performance. By contrast, the proposed method achieves considerably better online few-shot segmentation performance.
